text.p: Finnish cranes maker KCI Konecranes International Oy said in a statement on Wednesday it would include a redemption clause in its company bylaws to protect minority shareholders.

"Under the proposal, any shareholder, achieving a 33-1/3 percent ownership in the company will have to make an offer for all outstanding shares, at terms comparable to those he himself has paid," Konecranes said.
The offer would have to be renewed at 50 percent ownership, Konecranes said.
Konecranes the change was inspired by international rules.
"As corresponding rules do not apply in Finland, the board proposes to include the rules in the articles," it said.
Konecranes earlier released its preliminary 1996 report, which showed a 208 million markka profit after financial items, up from 135 million in 1995.
